questions.stem: A candidate's nursing board exam ends at question 85. What does this mean?

options.text: The result can't be told from the length
The exam had a technical error

questions.explanation: C is correct: the exam stopped at 85 because the computer was confident, either way, so the length doesn't show pass or fail. A and B assume the length tells the result. D: stopping at 85 is a normal end point, not an error.

questions.stem: Which statement about the nursing board exam's scoring is correct?
questions.explanation: B is correct: the exam is pass or fail, and you never see a percent score. A and C describe a percent score, which isn't given. D is wrong because the comparison is to the passing standard, not to classmates.

questions.stem: How many questions can a candidate receive on the nursing board exam?
questions.explanation: C is correct: the exam gives between 85 and 150 questions. A is too short a range. B was an older range that is no longer used. D is wrong because the adaptive exam's length varies.

questions.stem: A candidate plans to take two long breaks. Which statement shows correct understanding of exam time?
questions.explanation: B is correct: the exam allows up to 5 hours, and breaks count toward that time. A and D are wrong because breaks don't pause or extend the clock. C is wrong because there is a 5-hour limit.

questions.stem: A candidate gets a question right during computerized adaptive testing. What happens next?

options.text: The next question is a little harder
The next question is a little easier
The next question is the same difficulty

questions.explanation: A is correct: when you get a question right, the next one is a little harder. B happens after a wrong answer. C is wrong because one right answer doesn't end the exam. D is wrong because the adaptive test changes difficulty after each answer.

questions.stem: When does the adaptive exam stop?

options.text: When it is 95% sure the candidate is clearly above or below the passing standard
When the candidate gets 10 questions wrong in a row

questions.explanation: B is correct: the exam stops when it's 95% sure you're clearly above or clearly below the passing standard. A is wrong because it can run up to 150. C isn't a stopping rule. D: time is a limit, but the usual stop is the confidence rule.

questions.stem: A candidate says, "The questions keep getting harder, so I must be failing." What is the best response?

options.text: "Hard questions are normal and can even be a good sign."
"Hard questions mean the exam will run to 150."
"Skip the hard ones and come back."

questions.explanation: B is correct: the adaptive test gets harder after right answers, so hard questions are normal and can be a good sign. A assumes failure. C is wrong because difficulty doesn't set the length. D is wrong because candidates cannot skip questions or go back.

questions.stem: How are the next-generation case studies structured?

options.text: Three case studies, each with six questions
Six case studies, each with three questions

questions.explanation: B is correct: you get three case studies, each with six questions, for 18 items. A and C don't match that structure. D is wrong because the exam includes case studies, not only stand-alone items.

questions.stem: Which are next-generation item formats described in the video? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A, B, C, and D are correct: formats include bow-tie, matrix grids, trends, select all that apply, and drop-downs. E and F are not formats on the exam.

questions.stem: In the six clinical judgment steps, which step comes right after "analyze cues"?
questions.explanation: B is correct: the order is recognize cues, analyze cues, prioritize hypotheses, generate solutions, take action, evaluate outcomes. A comes before analyze cues. C and D come later.
